item.title: The rise of international acts and what it really means for SA talent
item.description: If you look at the South African gig calendar over the last few years, you would be forgiven for thinking that we have quietly become a permanent stop on the global touring circuit. Travis Scott at Calabash, Sting at SunBet Arena, Bryan Adams, Foreigner, and a long list of others. So, the obvious question is: is this good or bad for local talent? The answer is both. item.title: Nigeria: CKay’s Love Nwantiti surpasses 1bn Spotify streams
item.description: Nigerian musician CKay has reached a major milestone, with his track ‘Love Nwantiti’ surpassing one billion streams on Spotify. The achievement makes him one of the few African artists to reach the mark and the first Nigerian solo act to do so on the platform. Released in 2019 on the EP CKay the First, the song began as a modest regional hit before gaining widespread international attention. item.title: Open call: AmaGroove Residency 2026 in SA
item.description: The organisers of the AmaGroove Residency have announced an open call for artists to participate in the programme’s third edition, scheduled to take place from 22 to 29 March 2026 at Kromdraai Impact Hub in South Africa. Established as a collaborative platform for musicians and producers from South Africa and abroad, AmaGroove aims to support creative experimentation, cultural exchange and long-term artistic development. item.title: Shazam unveils feature spotlighting songs’ top moments
item.description: Shazam has announced a new feature aimed at enhancing music discovery by identifying the moments within tracks that generate the most listener interest. The tool, called Popular Segments, was rolled out on Shazam.com on 10 December. According to Shazam, the feature highlights sections of songs that prompted the highest volume of Shazam activity over the previous week. item.title: 2025 GQ Men of the Year Awards in SA: All the honourees
item.description: The 2025 GQ Men of the Year Awards were held at the Fairlawns Boutique Hotel in Johannesburg, South Africa on 10 December to recognise leading figures across music, sport, business, and culture. In the music category, Africori-signed artist Sjava received the Excellence in Music Award, following the release of his September project Uyena. item.title: South African Music Awards 2025: All the winners
item.description: The 2025 South African Music Awards were held at Gallagher Estate in Johannesburg on 13 December, with Goldmax and Thandiswa Mazwai securing major titles alongside multiple category wins. Goldmax claimed Album of the Year for Play At Your Own Risk, which also won Best Gqom Album. The release further underpinned his success on the night as he was named Male Artist of the Year, marking one of the strongest showings at the ceremony. item.title: SA: Sun-El Musician shares fourth studio album Under the Sun
item.description: South African producer and composer Sun-El Musician has released his fourth studio album, Under the Sun, marking his latest full-length release featuring a wide range of local and international collaborators. The album brings together long-standing collaborators Msaki, Ami Faku and Mthunzi, alongside artists including Zakes Bantwini, Chronical Deep, Youngr, Heavy-K, Thakzin, Manana, Nasty C and Deborah Cox. item.title: Apple Music launches Music That Moves Me highlighting African artists
item.description: Apple Music has launched Music That Moves Me, a campaign highlighting the intersection of music, movement and personal identity through the perspectives of Africa’s leading artists and athletes. The initiative features two playlist series. Warm Up showcases selections curated by professional footballers, including South African striker Lyle Foster and Nigerian midfielder Alex Iwobi, providing insight into the tracks they rely on to prepare mentally and physically for competition. item.title: Open call: DSAC Mzansi Golden Economy grant funding
item.description: The National Department of Sport, Arts and Culture (DSAC) has opened applications for grant funding under the Mzansi Golden Economy (MGE) programme, inviting submissions from organisations operating in the arts, culture and heritage sectors. item.title: Zim Hip Hop Awards 2025: All the winners
item.description: The Zim Hip Hop Awards were held at Zimbali Gardens in Harare, Zimbabwe on 13 December, with Bling 4 emerging as one of the most recognised rappers in the country. Bling 4 won Best Male and contributing to Song of the Year for ‘Boyz Rangu’, a collaboration with Runna Rulez. Runna Rulez also secured the People’s Choice Award, reflecting strong audience support.
